apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: my-alpine-deploy
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: my-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: my-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: my-container
        image: alpine
        command: ["sh", "-c", "while true; do echo working && sleep 10; done"]

metadata:
  name: my-alpine-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:

    kind: Deployment
    name: my-alpine-deploy
  minReplicas: 1
  maxReplicas: 10
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      targetAverageUtilization: 50

input: Hi, can you help me set up a simple blog website? Maybe 2 machines so it wont crash when many people visit.

said.result:
Your WordPress blog is running. Two copies of the site share one database, so if one copy crashes the other keeps serving visitors. To open it, run `kubectl -n bench-claude port-forward svc/blog 8080:80`, go to http://localhost:8080 and fill in the setup page to create your admin account.

I tested it and the site answers with that setup page. Your computer has only one machine in it (Docker Desktop), so both copies run on that one machine and they don't protect you if the computer itself goes down. Pictures you upload are saved inside one copy only, so a page can show a broken image when the other copy serves it, and they're lost when that copy restarts. Your posts are stored safely on disk. The setup file is `blog.yaml` in your working folder.
